newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Four groups hold 60 pct of Corimon.
newsitem.headline: Four groups hold 60 pct of Corimon.

text.p: Four Venezuelan investment groups have taken positions in paints and packaging company Corimon totaling 60 percent of its stock, Corimon President Francisco Layrisse said in a published interview.
Layrisse told the local daily El Nacional that the four groups had acquired stakes of 15 percent each in recent weeks.

The investors are Eduardo Gomez Sigala, president of the foods division of family-held Empresas Polar; local bank Interbank; Activalores brokerage; and the Neumann-Errard group led by industrialist Hans Neumann who was Corimon's largest shareholder.

Financial difficulties at U.S. and Argentine subsidiaries in early 1996 saw Corimon suspended from trading on the New York and Caracas stock exchanges and forced the company to undergo a massive restructuring that saw creditors take on most of the company's debts.
Layrisse said that although the company has made a strong recovery, its market capitalization is now just $170 million, compared to $450 million three years ago.
"Corimon sold 6.3 million gallons of paint last year, but it used to sell 13 million gallons in the past," he said.
